To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the literature-based curriculum was less sensitive than the traditional basal curriculum for the measurement of growth in reading.
passage probes selected for the literature-based basal reading series were less sensitive than probes selected from the traditional reading series to indexing growth in reading achievement over time.
the sensitivity of CBM probes was affected by the type of basal reading series from which they were drawn.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the effects of curriculum-based measurement (CBA), which is an assessment method designed to provide teachers with information about the growth of students' skills in reading, spelling, and mathematics.
the effects of curriculum and instructional practices on the sensitivity of curriculum-based measurement in reading.
the effects of basal reading programs on the sensitivity of CBM in reading.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
curriculum-based measurement passage probes selected from a traditional reading series may be more sensitive in indexing growth over time for students who are reading at the third-grade level.
the sensitivity of CBM is influenced by the curriculum in which the students are being instructed.
CBM passage probes selected from a literature-based basal reading series were less sensitive than probes selected from a traditional basal reading series.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of CBM passage probes selected from traditional basal reading programs will yield the most reliable and valid estimates of student progress in reading.
curriculum-based measurement (and, in particular, the use of curriculum-based measurement in reading) is a powerful tool in the hands of educators.
the use of curriculum-based measurement in reading should be done with caution.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the choice of CBM probes should be made carefully, as the probes used may not be sensitive to indexing growth in students who receive instruction using a curriculum that differs substantially from the curriculum for which the probes were designed.
curriculum selection should be a critical component of the design of CBM assessments, especially when the curriculum is used as a basis for selecting the passages to be administered.

the selection of CBM probes should be based on a student's instructional program, and that the selection of probes from a student's instructional series is more important to consider than the selection of probes based on the student's reading achievement level.
